R1 made no changes because its two tokens already appeared in the inherited entry. Jan now supplies a genuinely missing Infectum box and a proposed habitual Infectum-wa box.

Mxabarle u faṭəryarxo has an overt unmarked human notifyee; d mxabri u faṭəryarxo repeats that recipient frame in a projected decision. This is the same II.1 notification meaning, not a separate contact sense drawn from machine English.

mxabarwole li dawle contrasts a masculine message suffix with a feminine state recipient, favoring a message-object analysis. The following repeated behavior and d musakwo favor Infectum-wa, but the homographic -wo-le agent alternative remains for confirmation.
No independent fixed collocation is established with patriarch or state; no idiom is proposed.

Confirm mxabar-wo-le in Jan 3.15/170 as Infectum-wa plus message object, rather than Preterit-wa plus agent; habitual discourse supports the current proposed placement but does not by itself prove morphology.

Reporting minor remarks to the state can have an adverse consequence for their speakers, but recipient and message remain ordinary notification arguments. No independent denounce sense is required from this one context.
